$comment: Source for /trust/subprocessors. Every row names the repo files that call the provider (evidence) and the provider's own published terms (terms). tests/trust-page.test.js fails if an evidence path stops existing. Re-review when a provider key is added to or removed from the three-ws-api Cloud Run service, then bump lastReviewed.
method: Built from the environment variable names on the production Cloud Run service three-ws-api (names only, never values) and the code that reads each one. A key that is set but not called from a production request path is not listed.

groups.title: Infrastructure
groups.intro: Where the service runs and where account data and content are stored.

groups.title: AI model providers
groups.intro: Receive prompts, images or audio only when a user runs a feature that calls them. Self-hosted models on our own Google Cloud GPU workers are not third parties and are not listed.

groups.title: Blockchain access
groups.intro: Read and submit public chain data. Wallet addresses and transactions are public by nature.

groups.title: Communications
groups.intro: Email to users and private alerts to the operator.

subprocessors.name: Google Cloud
subprocessors.purpose: Application hosting (Cloud Run), scheduled jobs (Cloud Scheduler), request and error logs (Cloud Logging), cache and rate-limit store (Memorystore for Redis, private network only), secrets (Secret Manager), cold-storage archive and avatar reconstructions (Cloud Storage), self-hosted 3D and vision GPU workers.
data: All data the API processes in memory

subprocessors.name: Neon
subprocessors.purpose: Managed PostgreSQL, the primary database for accounts, agents, sessions, usage and payments records.
data: Account data (email, wallet addresses, password hashes)

subprocessors.name: Cloudflare
subprocessors.purpose: Object storage and public delivery for user files (R2): avatars, generated 3D models, uploads.

subprocessors.name: Privy
subprocessors.purpose: Optional social and email sign-in with embedded wallets. Used only when a user picks a Privy sign-in method.

subprocessors.name: Groq
subprocessors.purpose: Default chat inference lane (first in the failover order).

subprocessors.name: OpenRouter
subprocessors.purpose: Chat inference failover lane, routed to free-tier models.
subprocessors.region: Provider-managed; the downstream model host varies per request

subprocessors.name: NVIDIA
subprocessors.purpose: Chat inference failover lane, speech recognition, Audio2Face lip-sync, and the hosted Microsoft TRELLIS text-to-3D lane (NVIDIA API catalog and NVCF).

subprocessors.name: OpenAI
subprocessors.purpose: Paid chat backstop when every free lane is unavailable, and text embeddings for search and memory.

subprocessors.name: Google Vertex AI
subprocessors.purpose: Gemini chat anchor at the end of the failover order and Imagen image generation, billed to our own Google Cloud project.

subprocessors.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
subprocessors.purpose: Image understanding and a text inference lane.

subprocessors.name: Helius
subprocessors.purpose: Solana RPC: balances, transaction submission and chain indexing.

subprocessors.name: Alchemy
subprocessors.purpose: EVM RPC: balances and transaction reads on secondary EVM chains.

subprocessors.name: Pinata
subprocessors.purpose: IPFS pinning for metadata a user chooses to register on-chain. Pinned content is public by design.
data: Agent registration metadata the user publishes

subprocessors.name: Resend
subprocessors.purpose: Transactional email (sign-in links, receipts, notices) and operator alert email.

subprocessors.name: Telegram
subprocessors.purpose: Private operator alert channel for production faults. Alerts can carry request URLs and client IP addresses; it is never a public channel.
data: Error details, request URLs, client IP addresses
